questions.tag: United States of America · Central bank policy
questions.q: What action did the Federal Reserve take in its recent meeting?
o: It raised interest rates for the first time in three years.
It lowered interest rates to support the Nasdaq.
It kept borrowing costs unchanged at 3.75%.
it halted all sales of long-dated government debt.
questions.e: The central bank raised interest rates for the first time in three years despite political pushback. Lowering rates or keeping them flat describes other central banks or incorrect choices from different countries in the text.

questions.q: How did US stock futures and the Nasdaq react immediately after the Federal Reserve's rate decision?
o: They rallied and recovered in premarket trading.
They fell sharply alongside rising crude oil prices.
They remained entirely flat due to political uncertainty.
They halted all trading sessions pending further data.
questions.e: US stock futures rallied and the Nasdaq recovered in premarket trading as oil prices fell concurrently. Falling oil prices eased immediate cost pressures, which helped risk assets despite tighter monetary policy.

questions.q: What decision did the Bank of England make regarding its main policy rate?
o: It maintained the policy rate at 3.75%.
It raised borrowing costs by 0.75 points.
It cut interest rates to 1.25%.
It aligned its rate directly with the US Federal Reserve.
questions.e: The Bank of England maintained the policy rate at 3.75%, though three policymakers voted for an increase. This confirms the rate stayed unchanged rather than moving up or down.

questions.q: What structural change did the Bank of England make to its quantitative easing unwind plan?
o: It halted sales of long-dated gilts as inflation increased to 3.1%.
It accelerated long-dated debt sales to combat falling retail costs.
It permanently ended all corporate bond issuance.
It began buying foreign currency debt to support the pound.
questions.e: The Bank of England halted long-dated gilt sales, rewriting its quantitative easing unwind schedule when inflation printed at 3.1%. It did not accelerate sales or end corporate issuance.

questions.q: How did the German DAX index perform following the Federal Reserve's policy announcement?
o: It advanced to an over one-week high, opening 0.77% higher.
It dropped sharply as energy costs overwhelmed industrial firms.
It closed unchanged as investors awaited domestic employment data.
It fell by 2.9% following surprise rate cuts.
questions.e: The DAX advanced to an over one-week high, opening 0.77% higher following the Federal Reserve decision. It did not drop or close flat.

questions.q: What drove the acceleration of German inflation to 2.9%?
o: Advancing energy components within the consumer basket.
Sudden supply cuts in crude oil from Saudi Aramco.
Higher borrowing costs mandated by the European Central Bank.
Massive wage increases across the semiconductor sector.
questions.e: German inflation printed at 2.9% due to advancing energy components within the consumer basket. Saudi Aramco and semiconductor wages are unrelated or located in different regions in the text.

questions.q: What expectations did financial markets price in regarding the Bank of Japan?
o: A rate hike to 1.25%.
An immediate suspension of all debt refinancing operations.
A complete elimination of stablecoin pilots.
A pegging of the Yen to the US dollar.
questions.e: Market pricing fully anticipated a Bank of Japan rate hike to 1.25%. Stablecoins and debt refinancing involve different entities and do not represent the priced rate expectations.

questions.q: What project was discussed between Japan and the US as part of their investment pact?
o: A GlobalFoundries chip plant.
A nationwide stablecoin network.
A massive rare earth drilling joint venture.
A cross-border real estate investment trust.
questions.e: Japan and the US discussed a GlobalFoundries chip plant within their $550bn investment pact. Rare earth drilling and real estate trusts belong to other companies and countries.

questions.q: How did Chinese firms raise or register new corporate debt according to the reports?
o: SDIC Power filed a shelf registration for up to 8 billion yuan, and CGN Power raised 1 billion yuan.
Xiaomi borrowed 8 billion yuan to finance laptop price hikes.
Li Auto issued 500,000 yuan in government bonds.
Reborn Chicecream sold 1 billion yuan in long-dated gilts.
questions.e: An SDIC Power subsidiary scheduled a registration for up to 8 billion yuan, while CGN Power raised 1 billion yuan via a five-year corporate issuance. Xiaomi and Reborn Chicecream adjusted consumer product prices rather than issuing sovereign debt.

questions.q: How did Li Auto price its new SUV relative to the broader market segment?
o: It launched the i9 at 369,800 yuan, undercutting the wider 500,000-yuan segment.
It priced the vehicle at 8 billion yuan to match corporate debt filings.
It matched competitor laptop prices across seven distinct SKUs.
It increased the price to over one million yuan due to energy costs.
questions.e: Li Auto positioned its i9 SUV at 369,800 yuan to undercut the broader 500,000-yuan segment. The other choices incorrectly mix up debt figures, laptop SKUs, or imaginary price hikes.

questions.q: What operation did the Reserve Bank of India execute on September 17, 2026?
o: An open market bond sale accepting ₹50,000 crore.
A total cancellation of all non-banking financial licences.
A complete ban on crude oil imports from Saudi Arabia.
A reduction of the benchmark rate to 3.75%.
questions.e: The Reserve Bank of India executed an open market bond sale accepting ₹50,000 crore from total bids. It did not ban crude imports or change benchmark rates in this specific operation.

questions.q: Why did several non-banking financial companies lose their registration with the Reserve Bank of India?
o: Five had their certificates revoked under statutory provisions, and eight surrendered them voluntarily upon exiting the sector.
All 13 companies failed to buy government securities maturing in 2032.
They were forced to merge with Saudi Aramco after crude supplies halted.
They breached foreign exchange limits during open market bond auctions.
questions.e: The Reserve Bank of India revoked five registrations under statutory provisions, while eight entities surrendered their licences voluntarily after exiting the business. They did not lose them over bond auctions or mergers with oil companies.

questions.q: What action did Petrobras take regarding its domestic diesel prices?
o: It increased distributor diesel prices by 1 real per litre while applying matching fiscal discounts under a subsidy program.
It lowered diesel prices to zero to offset global inflation.
It suspended all fuel supplies to international buyers due to exploration contracts.
It fixed diesel prices permanently to match Computer Modelling Group software fees.
questions.e: Petrobras lifted average distributor diesel prices by 1 real per litre while concurrently applying matching discounts under an inflation-offsetting subsidy program. It did not eliminate prices or tie them to software licensing.

questions.q: What caused crude oil prices to surge past $105 per barrel?
o: Saudi Aramco suspended crude supplies to Indian refiners amid regional Gulf hostilities.
Wipro, Aramco, and SAP launched Wipro STO360 for industrial plants.
Brazil increased its production-sharing contracts for exploratory blocks.
The Federal Reserve executed its first interest rate hike in three years.
questions.e: Saudi Aramco suspended crude shipments to Indian refiners amid escalating Gulf hostilities, forcing buyers onto spot markets and pushing prices past $105. Software launches, Brazilian oil blocks, and US rate hikes did not cause this direct feedstock cutoff.

questions.q: What is the purpose of Wipro STO360, launched by Wipro, Aramco, and SAP?
o: To streamline shutdown, turnaround, and outage management at industrial plants using artificial intelligence.
To replace crude oil pipelines with digital energy trading platforms.
To regulate non-banking financial companies in India.
To manage sovereign debt refinancing for Japanese real estate trusts.
questions.e: Wipro STO360 uses artificial intelligence to coordinate complex maintenance schedules and streamline shutdown, turnaround, and outage management at industrial plants. It has nothing to do with oil pipelines, Indian finance rules, or Japanese trusts.

questions.q: How did naira depreciation affect domestic banks according to Fitch?
o: It amplified the consolidated earnings contribution of foreign subsidiaries through balance-sheet translation gains.
It completely eliminated all foreign-denominated cash flows.
It forced the central bank to halt official spot-market clearing.
It reduced commercial demand for hard currency to zero.
questions.e: Sustained naira depreciation amplified the earnings contribution of offshore subsidiaries because foreign currency earnings expanded in domestic terms via translation gains. It did not eliminate cash flows or stop interbank clearing.

questions.q: What short-term trajectory did UOB project for the Australian Dollar against the US Dollar?
o: Downside momentum toward 0.7050.
An aggressive surge past 1.25% due to Bank of Japan tightening.
A direct pegging to the Nigerian naira.
A complete stabilization backed by Brazilian rare earth drilling.
questions.e: UOB analysts outlined short-term downside momentum toward 0.7050 against the US Dollar. The other choices involve unrelated currencies or commodities from different global regions.

questions.q: What operational updates were reported for Australian resource and technology firms?
o: Power Minerals advanced Brazilian rare earth drilling, Falcon Metals extended a gold system, and DXN secured high-performance computing contracts.
Orix JREIT raised 10.6 billion Yen to buy Australian gold mines.
Saudi Aramco took over all rare earth drilling operations in Sydney.
Xiaomi launched laptop SKUs to mine rare earth minerals.
questions.e: Power Minerals advanced rare earth drilling in Brazil, Falcon Metals extended the Blue Moon gold system, and DXN secured high-performance computing contracts for its AI data-centre pipeline. Japanese REITs, Saudi oil companies, and Chinese tech firms are entirely separate.

Retailers raised operating cost baselines.

Quantitative easing portfolios were fully unwound.
